concept.title: Basic selectors and namespaces
concept.shortdesc: Basic selectors match an element by its name, attributes or namespace. Combine selector parts when you want to require more than one condition.

section.title: Element names and any element
section.p: Selectors 4 §5.1, Type (tag name) selector; Selectors 4 §5.2, Universal selector.
A type selector is an element name, such as chapter or title. It matches elements with that name. The universal selector * matches any element.
An unprefixed name uses the default namespace declared with @namespace. Without a declared default namespace, it matches an element with no namespace.

section.title: IDs and classes
section.p: Selectors 4 §6.6, Class selectors; Selectors 4 §6.7, ID selectors.
An ID identifies an element. Write # followed by the ID value to select it. CSSMedia checks the id and xml:id attributes.

A class selector starts with a period, as in .warning. CSSMedia accepts this syntax, but does not use it to test an XML attribute. Selectors Level 4 leaves the meaning of class membership to the document language, and XML does not define one universal class attribute.
If your XML uses an unnamespaced class attribute containing space-separated class names, test it with an attribute selector. The ~= operator checks for one whole, space-separated value:
This matches an element whose class attribute contains warning as one of its values. It does not make .warning a working class selector in CSSMedia.

section.title: Attributes
section.p: An attribute selector checks an XML attribute. Put its name in square brackets to require that the attribute exists. Add an operator and value to compare its contents.

= compares the whole value. ~= checks for a space-separated word. |= matches the value itself or a value followed by a hyphen. ^=, $= and *= check for text at the start, end or anywhere in the value. The i flag ignores ASCII letter case. The s flag requests case-sensitive comparison.
An attribute selector without a namespace prefix checks an attribute with no namespace. Use a declared prefix to select an attribute in a namespace.

section.title: XML namespaces
section.p: CSS Namespaces 3 §3, Declaring namespaces: the @namespace rule.
XML elements and attributes can belong to namespaces. A CSS namespace declaration assigns a prefix to a namespace URI. Use that prefix in a selector to choose elements in that namespace.

svg|rect selects rect elements in the declared SVG namespace. *|rect selects rect elements in any namespace. |rect selects rect elements with no namespace. The CSS prefix is an alias for the URI. It does not need to match the prefix used in the XML.

A bare attribute selector such as [id] always selects an attribute with no namespace. An undeclared prefix makes that selector invalid. CSSMedia ignores a style rule if any selector in its selector list is invalid.
